situation (example wording): A follow-up turn: "female murder victims in Memphis in 2024", then "male"; "same for 2023"; "make it a rate"; "what about Dallas"
what the app does today: P22 (a button changes only its choice) and P23 ("What about Dallas?" keeps today's behavior); no general rule for follow-ups.
proposed behavior: The previous turn and the follow-up are rewritten into one complete standalone question ("Male murder victims in Memphis in 2024"). It is shown above the answer and the user can edit it; an edited question runs as a new question. The rewritten question goes through the usual reading, plan and delivery, with no separate follow-up path. If the rewrite is uncertain or ambiguous, ask instead of guessing. Edits that only change the presentation (bar or line, labels, colors, sort) never reach the data engine; the page's chart controls handle them. [Superseded by P157 (2026-11-19): the page has no such controls, so a chart change is declined.] Only the previous turn is used for now. The engine session's F1-F12 are guidance for the rewrite and a source of test cases, not rules (for example: replace a place unless "add", "compare to" or "and"; "remove 2026" shortens the period). Quarters and the population and agencies-reporting columns are their own rows (P71, P72).
exact default or choices offered: The rewritten question, shown and editable; ask when uncertain.
why: Follow-ups resist hard rules ("If I get female murder victims then I can ask for male, or ask for a line chart to be a bar chart"); showing the question the model answered lets the user check and correct it.
status: Decided 2026-10-31 (Jeff: "Yes. I like the idea of an editable response of what the model thinks was asked."; declined F1 as a hard rule); amended by P73 (a model's rewrite is proposed for confirmation); the chart and table edits are declined by P157 (2026-11-19) (cleanup 2026-11-22), audit B26
test cases: Tests that cite this row: scripts/test-nibrs-follow-up.ts, scripts/test-nibrs-model-rewriter.ts.
